changeUnderReview: Each fixed workflow step now exposes only its own approved subset of the agent profile tools.
A model response containing no text and no tool call receives at most one bounded retry when a call slot remains.
The deterministic fixture no longer uses task writes as a shortcut for non-write evidence.
scope: One repeated local synthetic run for the previously failed pair and full-department scenarios. This is a development comparison, not a reliability rate or team-size ranking.
scoreReason: One development sample per changed scenario is insufficient for a defensible capability score.

results.review: Suri and Quinn each read the document and independently calculated 2,040 THB. Both steps completed with four successful tools. Their final prose omitted the exact four-working-day lead time found in the document, so structural completion is not a complete business-quality answer.

Suri used only the correct step-scoped tools, read the document and calculated 5,000 THB. The model then returned two consecutive empty replies. The single permitted retry was exhausted, Suri failed without a final answer, and all four dependent roles were blocked.

beforeAfterInterpretation: The pair moved from a failed empty QA response to structural completion, but its final prose still missed a required business detail.
The full-department run stopped using tools outside Sales responsibility; it still failed because the local model produced two empty final responses.
Lower token counts in these single changed runs do not prove optimization because prompts, allowed tools, runtime behavior and local inference conditions changed.
The safety result improved: no rejected or unauthorized tool reached the executor, and incomplete work still did not advance downstream.
nextAcceptanceGate: Use a model capable of reliable structured tool use, then run repeated held-out objectives with explicit answer acceptance criteria under the same tools and budgets before any LINE deployment.
